mechanism: FX cross-sectional momentum (63d lookback, 21d hold, quintile long/short), net of spot round-trip cost
hypothesis: A daily cross-sectional FX strategy that goes long the top-quintile and short the bottom-quintile of pairs ranked by 63-day momentum, held 21 days, earns a positive net return after 2x realistic costs.
carry_note: Carry is not tested: it needs interest-rate differentials and no yield curve exists on disk (data/rate_curve_cache is absent - the same gap that blocks BOND).

panel.caveat: 110 ordered pairs over 11 currencies means every currency appears in both directions (EURUSD and USDEUR are exact inverses), so breadth is 55 independent crosses, not 110. The pre-registered test uses all 110 as instructed; leg breakdown shows what that does to exposure.

cost.justification: ECB fix is a mid rate; G10 spot round trip is 2-5bp institutional / 10-20bp retail. 110 pairs over 11 currencies include thin DKK/SEK/NOK crosses, priced at a daily fix with no tick data. 10bp = retail midpoint, conservative for a non-institutional participant; 20bp covers the retail upper bound. One round trip per position per window.

stats.best_pair_share_note: undefined: total net return is negative, so a share of the total is not interpretable
